# Plan: The Yantra App and the Drshya Design System

## 1. Overview

Yantra is CLI-only today. This plan builds the **Yantra app**: a local graphical app opened by
`yantra ui` in a Chrome app window, styled by **Drshya**, Yantra's own design system, and held level
with the CLI by construction. The design source is [`ui_brainstorm.md`](./ui_brainstorm.md)
(Session 5); the visual reference is
[Yantra Interface Study 01](https://claude.ai/artifact/46XfRuWQyypjqhS3B9xPQB), with the **Ion**
accent chosen. The plan was revised after
[`reviews/plan_critique_ui.md`](./reviews/plan_critique_ui.md); [§17](#17-critique-disposition)
maps every finding to the change that addresses it.

The plan has three parts:

1. **Foundations that also improve the CLI.**
   - A declarative command registry, with command handlers that take their terminal dependencies
     as explicit inputs.
   - Shared-resource locks.
   - One sequence-numbered run-event log with a commit and replay contract.
   - Run ownership: exclusive leases, a per-run local socket, and reconciliation of dead owners.

   These are protocol and core work. The CLI benefits on its own: concurrent settings writes stop
   losing changes, and a killed run is no longer "running" forever.

2. **A reliable local app host.** `yantra ui` starts a supervisor that serves the app on
   `127.0.0.1`. It launches each task exactly once as a **detached CLI worker process**, two at a
   time with the rest queued, and reattaches to them after any crash. The scheduler daemon is
   untouched and stays hard zero-LLM (memory → Architecture).
3. **The app.** Drshya (`packages/ui`) and `apps/web` provide:
   - run results and audit for every run;
   - a live run screen;
   - interventions with an atomic consent contract;
   - the live browser view;
   - a command palette;
   - generated surfaces, so every remaining command is usable on day one.

**In scope:** FEAT-061 to FEAT-072. **Explicitly deferred to Phase 2** and documented in
[§13](#13-phase-2-deferred-and-documented): live takeover (solving a captcha or login yourself in the
live view), an `ask_user` tool for missing information, desktop notifications for finished or failed
runs, live viewing of CLI-launched runs, Compact density, and the bespoke studios.

**Durability promise, stated precisely.** The plan guarantees _committed local records_. These are
run events and state written by Yantra, flushed at the points §8 defines. They survive the death of
any one Yantra process. The plan does not promise to know about website effects that no record
observed, nor durability across power loss between flush points.

## 3. Tech Stack Additions

The canonical stack is in `memory.md` → Tech Stack. These are additions for this plan. Per memory
(Dependencies), **the user approves each new dependency before it is pinned**; Feature specs pin
exact current stable versions at that point.

| Component                | Technology                                                                                                        | Justification                                                                                                  |
| ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| UI runtime               | `react`, `react-dom` (19.x)                                                                                       | Largest accessible-primitive ecosystem; React Aria is React-only. Session 1 direction.                         |
| Build                    | `vite`, `@vitejs/plugin-react`                                                                                    | Fast static build for a localhost app; no SSR need, so no Next.js.                                             |
| Routing and read caching | `@tanstack/react-router`, `@tanstack/react-query`                                                                 | Type-safe routes; cache, dedupe and invalidation for in-process reads.                                         |
| Primitives               | `react-aria-components`                                                                                           | Broadest accessible set: virtualized Table and GridList, Tree, drag and drop, DatePicker, i18n. User decision. |
| Styling                  | `tailwindcss` v4, `@tailwindcss/vite`, `tailwindcss-react-aria-components`, `tailwind-variants`, `tailwind-merge` | CSS-first `@theme` tokens; React Aria state variants; multi-slot component variants.                           |
| Icons                    | `lucide-react`                                                                                                    | ISC; used only behind the Drshya semantic icon registry.                                                       |
| Fonts                    | `@fontsource-variable/archivo`, `@fontsource-variable/martian-mono`                                               | Self-hosted (OFL); a local-first app makes no third-party requests.                                            |
| Markdown in results      | `react-markdown` with `remark-gfm`, raw HTML disabled                                                             | Brief `sections[].body_md` and template documents; no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`.                               |
| WebSocket server         | `ws`                                                                                                              | Node 24 has no built-in WebSocket server. HTTP uses `node:http`; run sockets use `node:net`.                   |
| Component tests          | `@testing-library/react` (with the repo's existing jsdom)                                                         | Instrument behavior tests under Vitest.                                                                        |
| Accessibility checks     | `axe-core`                                                                                                        | Automated rule checks in the gallery and app e2e, alongside manual screen-reader passes.                       |
| Visual regression        | `pixelmatch`, `pngjs`                                                                                             | Screenshots taken with the existing `puppeteer-core`; no second browser driver.                                |

**Already present and reused:** `proper-lockfile` (core) for every new lock; the browser
`process-identity` and `process-lifecycle` modules for process identity and tree termination.

**Deliberately not added:** Storybook (in-app gallery route), Playwright (puppeteer-core already
drives Chrome), Motion (CSS and View Transitions cover the MVP), a state-management library
(`useSyncExternalStore` over the event stream), Express or Fastify, shadcn/ui or any pre-styled kit
(memory → General, Drshya rule).

## 4. Decisions

Decisions D1–D10 come from the planning checkpoints on 2026-11-02. D7 and D10 were revised, and
D11–D18 added, after the plan critique the same day.

- **D1 — Separate app host; the daemon is unchanged.** Memory makes scheduled and daemon runs hard
  zero-LLM, and `daemon-runtime.ts` enforces it. Serving the app from the daemon would make `do` and
  agentic research impossible from the app. `yantra ui` therefore starts its own host for attended
  work. The app shows schedules and parked runs, reads daemon state through `FileDaemonLock.probe()`,
  and resolves parked runs through the `confirm` command's shared core service (D12).
- **D2 — Supervisor plus CLI workers; reads in-process.** The host never executes a task. Run-class
  and mutating commands run as worker processes that execute the **same command handler** as the
  terminal through a worker adapter (FEAT-072). Reads use core read functions in the host process.
  **Exception:** credential writes run in-process through the core keychain function `secret set`
  uses, so a secret never appears in a process argument list.
- **D3 — Detached workers own a per-run socket; any host can reattach.** Workers are spawned
  detached, shell-free, with an explicit argv array, and they outlive the host. Each worker serves its
  run on a local socket recorded in an owner-only lease. A restarted host finds live leases, performs
  the handshake (D17), replays from `run-events.jsonl`, and follows live.
- **D4 — Two concurrent app run slots; the rest queue.** At most two app invocations are **reserved
  or running** at any moment, enforced under a slot lock (D11). CLI-launched runs are shown but not
  throttled. Queued items start only through D11's reservation, never on host restart by themselves.
- **D5 — Attendance, not host liveness, governs unattended waits.**
  - **Who counts as attending:**
    - an **app window** with a live, authenticated WebSocket that is subscribed to interventions
      and has sent an attendance heartbeat within the last 30 seconds;
    - for terminal-launched runs, the **controlling terminal**, as today.
  - **What does not count:** a live host with zero windows, a non-empty queue, or a parked
    scheduled run.
  - **The ceiling.** While an intervention is pending and no one is attending, a **cumulative
    unattended ceiling of 15 minutes** runs. Reconnecting pauses it and never resets it, so a
    flapping connection cannot extend the wait.
  - **The effective deadline** is the minimum of:
    - the request's `timeout_ms`;
    - `agent.confirm_timeout` for agentic runs (default 3 minutes);
    - the run's remaining wall clock;
    - the ceiling.

    The ceiling applies even when `timeout_ms` is `null`, so no unattended run waits indefinitely.

  - **Expiry** resolves the request as `timed_out` (`decided_by: timeout`, reason `unattended`). The
    run then exits cleanly as a handoff (exit 4) with the item recorded.
  - **Sleep and wake.** Deadlines are absolute instants. On wake, an expired deadline resolves
    before any late answer is accepted.

- **D6 — Host death does not stop runs.** Workers continue and try to complete; only an
  intervention falls back to D5.
- **D7 (revised) — Execution state is separate from task outcome.** A run whose owner died gets
  `executionState: interrupted`, recorded separately from its outcome.
  - **Outcome** follows the evidence: `partial` if a result was persisted, otherwise `failed`. It
    is **never** `aborted`, which means the user interrupted.
  - **New enum variant.** `TerminationReason` gains `owner_lost`. The current closed enum has no
    such value, and the first draft's "older readers stay valid" claim was wrong.
  - **Compatibility.** New code reads every existing artifact. **Older executables cannot read new
    enum values** (`owner_lost`, `user_app`). That is an accepted pre-release limit: forward
    readability is preserved, backward is not (memory → General, artifact compatibility).
  - **Fixtures** cover both directions.
- **D8 — Design decisions carried from the brainstorm.**
  - Ion accent; Chrome app window; React Aria Components.
  - Design system name **Drshya**, published as `@yantra/ui`.
  - Glass for controls only, with Solid mode.
  - The command registry lives in `@yantra/protocol` and generates commander, not the reverse.
  - Gallery as an in-app development route.
- **D9 — Phase 2 is explicit.**
  - Live takeover, `ask_user`, finished/failed desktop notifications, live viewing of CLI runs,
    Compact density and the bespoke studios are documented in §13.
  - Desktop notifications for **"needs you"** items stay in the MVP, as best-effort delivery tracked
    separately from decisions (D12).
- **D10 (revised) — UI window browser and failure.**
  - **Browser order:** an installed system Chromium supporting `--app` (Chrome, then Edge). Chrome
    for Testing shows a "for automated testing only" infobar, so the resolved Yantra browser comes
    after those.
  - **No Chromium found:** `yantra ui` exits **3** with the remediation (`yantra browser install`)
    **and** prints the app URL so it can be opened manually.
  - **`--print`:** always prints the URL and exits 0.
  - **Profile:** the window uses its own profile, never an automation instance or profile.
- **D11 — Launch ownership: invocations are deduplicated and slots are reserved durably.** Each app
  submission carries a client-generated **invocation ID** (idempotency key).
  - **Record.** The host creates `ui/invocations/<invocation_id>.json` with an exclusive create. A
    repeated submission of the same ID returns the existing record's state and never launches
    twice.
  - **States.** `queued → reserved → spawning → claimed → running → finished`, plus `never_started`,
    `start_unknown`, `needs_review` and `discarded`.
  - **Reserving a slot.** This happens under the slot lock and allocates the run ID before spawn.
  - **The worker claims.** Under the same lock, its first action moves the record from
    `reserved`/`spawning` to `claimed` and records its process identity. It then exclusively creates
    the run's `lease.json`. It does nothing else before the claim. A worker that finds the record
    `never_started` or `discarded` exits without side effects.
  - **Recovery after a host crash** (also under the lock):
    - unclaimed `reserved`/`spawning` becomes `never_started`, and Start is enabled;
    - `claimed` with a live, identity-verified owner is attached;
    - `claimed` with a dead owner is reconciled (FEAT-064);
    - an owner identity that cannot be verified becomes `start_unknown`. Start then requires explicit
      confirmation with a possible-duplicate-effects warning.
  - **Resume of an existing run** uses the run's exclusive lease, so two resumes can never own one
    run.
  - **What this guarantees:** deduplicated launching. It does not guarantee exactly-once website
    effects after an arbitrary worker crash.
- **D12 — Consent authority and action binding.**
  - **Live runs.** The worker owning the run is the **sole decision authority**. Every answer path
    (app windows, `yantra confirm`, the terminal, timeout) goes through one atomic transition on the
    worker's event loop. That transition checks that the item is still pending and the deadline has
    not passed, persists and flushes the decision, and only then replies or continues.
  - **Responses:**
    - `accepted`;
    - `already_decided {decision, decided_by, decided_at}`. A duplicate after reconnect gets this,
      so answers are idempotent from the client's view.
    - `expired {decided_at}`;
    - `stale` (unknown ID or an earlier attempt).
  - **Parked runs (no live owner).** A decision is claimed by exclusive create of
    `runs/<id>/decisions/<confirmation_id>.json`, which is atomic on every OS, before
    `confirmations.jsonl` is appended. `yantra confirm` and the Inbox share this core service.
  - **Binding.** A grant is bound to `{run_id, step_id, action_kind, target_host, plan_digest,
step_digest}`. These are new optional fields on `ConfirmationRequest`.
  - **The resume gateway** replaces `PreGrantedConfirmationGateway`. It grants **only** a request
    whose binding matches exactly. A mismatch is denied with the blocker "The step changed since you
    approved it." A second flagged step after resume is denied, as today, and surfaced as a handoff.
  - **Provenance on replay.** The original decision's `decided_by` and `decided_at` are kept, and a
    `replayed_at` field is added.
- **D13 — Requested invocation versus execution receipt.**
  - **`CommandInvocation`** is what was requested: command path, argv, explicit `cwd`, invocation ID.
  - **Execution receipt.** At start every run (CLI, worker, daemon) writes `execution-receipt.json`.
    It holds:
    - effective **non-secret** settings, each with its source: flag, the env var's **name**,
      preference or default;
    - content identities: workflow and template path plus SHA-256;
    - the browser selection;
    - the Yantra version and `cwd`.

    The full environment and credentials are never recorded.

  - **When settings resolve.** At **start**. When a queued item reaches a free slot, the host
    re-resolves read-only. If the result differs from the snapshot the composer showed at
    submission, the item becomes `needs_review` (an Inbox item) instead of starting. The choices are
    _Start with current settings_, _Start with the settings I submitted_ (pinned as explicit flags
    where the registry allows) and _Discard_.
  - **Paths.** App invocations always carry an explicit `cwd` and absolute paths, so the host's own
    launch directory never matters.
  - **Environment.** Workers inherit the host's environment as captured when the host started.
    Health shows its age and offers "restart the app to pick up environment changes".
  - **Run again** uses current settings by default, or the prior receipt's settings on request.
  - **Historical runs without an invocation** are reconstructed from the manifest and labeled
    "Reconstructed". If that is impossible, the composer opens with the goal only.

- **D14 — Shared-resource locks.**
  - **Which writes are locked.** Every read-modify-write of `config.yaml`, `profile.yaml`, a
    workflow file, a template file or the schedule registry runs under a core, process-safe lock
    keyed to that resource (`proper-lockfile`).
  - **Temporary files** are unique (`<file>.<pid>.<random>.tmp`), replacing the shared `<path>.tmp`
    in `config/write.ts` and `profile/profile-file.ts`.
  - **A busy lock** is an explicit response (exit 3 with reason `busy`), never a silent overwrite.
  - **Coverage.** CLI processes use the same functions, so terminal and app writers coordinate.
  - **Managed browser installs** reuse the existing managed-browser reservations.
  - **A persistent workflow browser profile** admits one run at a time. A second run waits in the
    queue or gets `busy`.
- **D15 — Data-directory relocation is a reviewed app exemption.** Relocation moves the directory
  that holds the host's own lock, queue and sockets, so it cannot run under a live host.
  - The app's Data surface shows the current location and the exact steps: close the app, run
    `yantra config data-dir <path>`, run `yantra ui`.
  - The `config data-dir` guard keeps refusing while a host lock or a live lease exists.
- **D16 — The handler is the unit of parity.** Registry extraction alone does not make a command
  safe for a worker. FEAT-072 turns terminal coupling into explicit dependencies before any worker
  runs a command. Exceptional commands (`init`, `secret`, `config edit`, `browser install/update`,
  `open`, `confirm`, `daemon start/stop`, `ui`) get small explicit adapters instead of growing the
  registry into a UI language.
- **D17 — Version negotiation for independently living processes.**
  - **Handshake.** Run sockets and the host control socket begin with
    `hello {channel_version, capabilities}`. The server answers with its supported range.
  - **Incompatible worker.** If the host cannot speak a running worker's version, the run shows
    _"Started by Yantra <version>; live view unavailable. The run continues and its result will
    appear here."_ The host never aborts that worker.
  - **Unknown events** render in `EventInspector`.
  - **Stale web assets.** Assets are content-hashed. The app compares its build ID with the host's
    on every connect and reloads when idle if they differ.
- **D18 — Loopback threat model.**
  - **In scope:** web content in any browser on the machine (CSRF, DNS rebinding, cross-port cookie
    exposure); other loopback services; other OS users.
  - **Out of scope:** code already running as the same OS user (it can read `~/.yantra`) and
    physical access.
  - **Why a cookie is not enough.** Cookies are not isolated by port, so a cookie alone never
    authorizes anything. §7 defines the per-window capability that accompanies it.

- `apps/cli/src/commands/daemon-runtime.ts:109,153`: daemon fires and parked-run resumes never open

  nothing detects a dead owner (FEAT-064).
- † `packages/protocol/src/schemas/task-outcome.ts:25`: `TerminationReason` is a closed enum without
  an interruption value (D7).
- † `apps/cli/src/commands/confirm.ts`: `hasDecision` and `appendDecision` are separate operations,
  not an atomic first-writer rule (D12).
- † `packages/core/src/scheduler/pregranted-confirmation-gateway.ts`: grants the first request it
  receives without comparing it to the approved one; already denies a second flagged step (D12).
- † `packages/core/src/config/write.ts:48` and `packages/core/src/profile/profile-file.ts:197`: both
  write through a fixed `<path>.tmp` (D14).
- † `packages/core/src/browser/sensitive-screen-latch.ts`: set before an agent secret dispatch,
  cleared by a verified top-level epoch change or teardown; no deterministic executor or workflow
  path uses it (FEAT-069).
- † `packages/core/src/browser/process-identity.ts` and `process-lifecycle.ts`: start-token process
  identity, `NodeProcessTreeTerminator` and `BrowserProcessSupervisor` already exist (FEAT-064).
- † `packages/core/src/workflow/replay/types.ts`: a run outcome's `brief` is optional (FEAT-066).
- `packages/agent/src/runtime/orchestrator.ts:1262,1327`: an agentic handoff is terminal with
  `blocker` and `safestNextAction` (FEAT-068).
- `packages/agent/src/runtime/connector.ts`: `AgentProgressEvent` lives in `@yantra/agent`, while
  `TaskEvent` lives in protocol (FEAT-063).
- `packages/agent/src/runtime/confirmation-bridge.ts:75-89`: interactive waits are bounded by
  `agent.confirm_timeout` and wall clock; non-interactive connectors time out at once (D5).
- `packages/core/src/scheduler/notify.ts`: `SinkNotifier` writes `notifications.jsonl` and sends a
  best-effort desktop notification (FEAT-068).

## 6. Interface Design

### Four distinct contracts

Following the critique's adaptiveness recommendation, four contracts stay separate:

1. **Requested invocation** (`CommandInvocation`, FEAT-062).
2. **Effective execution receipt** (`execution-receipt.json`, FEAT-072).
3. **Durable run state and events** (lease, `run-events.jsonl`, manifest; FEAT-063/064).
4. **Surface presentation metadata** (registry presentation fields plus app-side adapters;
   FEAT-062/070).

Executors never embed browser UX, and new connectors can be added without touching surfaces.

### CLI surface

- **`yantra ui [--print] [--json]`** (new). Starts the host if none is live, then opens the app
  window with a fresh launch code (D10). `--json` emits `{schemaVersion, url, port, hostPid, reused}`.
  Exit codes: 0 opened or printed; 3 environment (no Chromium, bind failure, lock contention); 1
  validation.
- **`yantra confirm <run-id> <grant|deny>`** (extended). For a live run it answers through the
  run's socket and gets a D12 response. For a parked run it uses the atomic decision claim. Output
  states which case applied.
- **`yantra prefs set ui.theme|ui.surfaces`** (new `profile.yaml` keys). `theme` is
  `system|light|dark`; `surfaces` is `glass|solid`. **`ui.density` is not added until Phase 2**: a
  preference with one usable value would be a dead control (memory → General).
- **Busy responses.** Commands that write a locked resource can now exit 3 with reason `busy`
  (D14).
- **No other user-visible change.** The worker entry point is internal (`apps/cli/dist/worker.js`)
  and is not a flag.

### Execution classes (registry field `execution`, which may depend on options)

| Command                                                                                                                                                                                                  | Class                              | Notes                                                                     |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ask`, `research`, `do`, `run`                                                                                                                                                                           | `run`                              | Detached worker, slot counted                                             |
| `resume`                                                                                                                                                                                                 | `run`                              | Exclusive lease on the existing run                                       |
| `browser check`                                                                                                                                                                                          | `run`                              | Launches an isolated probe browser                                        |
| `doctor`                                                                                                                                                                                                 | `read`; `run` with `--agent-smoke` | Option-dependent class                                                    |
| `browser install`, `browser update`                                                                                                                                                                      | `exclusive`                        | Existing managed-browser reservation; blocks run starts                   |
| `list`, `show`, `audit`, `report`, `usage`, `schedules`, `profile`, `config path/list/get/validate`, `model list`, `sites list`, `template list/show`, `daemon status`, `browser list`, `prefs get/list` | `read`                             | Host, in-process                                                          |
| `config set/unset`, `prefs set/approve`, `model add/rm/default`, `sites add/remove`, `template new/lint/save/remove`, `lint`, `schedule`, `unschedule`, `browser use`                                    | `mutate`                           | Short-lived worker; D14 locks                                             |
| `confirm`                                                                                                                                                                                                | `mutate` via the D12 service       | Inbox adapter                                                             |
| `secret set/rm/list`                                                                                                                                                                                     | `in-process-secure`                | Value never in argv; `list` names only                                    |
| `open`                                                                                                                                                                                                   | adapter                            | In-app result view; "Open in system app" runs `open` as a `mutate` worker |
| `init`                                                                                                                                                                                                   | adapter                            | FEAT-071 onboarding over the shared `init` service                        |
| `config edit`                                                                                                                                                                                            | adapter                            | Raw-YAML editor with `validate`, instead of launching `$EDITOR`           |
| `config data-dir`                                                                                                                                                                                        | exemption                          | D15                                                                       |
| `daemon start` / `daemon stop`                                                                                                                                                                           | adapter (`mutate`)                 | `stop` asks first                                                         |
| `ui`                                                                                                                                                                                                     | exemption                          | Never executed from inside the app                                        |

FEAT-062 enumerates every command and subcommand. The parity test fails on any command without a
class.

### `CommandInvocation` and the CLI twin

- Fields: `{invocation_id, path, argv, cwd}`.
- `parse(argv)` and `format(invocation, shell)` for `posix`, `powershell` and `cmd`. The default shell
  follows the host OS (PowerShell on Windows). An argument `cmd` cannot represent, such as a newline,
  makes the cmd format unavailable, and the app says so.
- Workers are spawned shell-free from `{path, argv}`. Formatting exists only for display and Copy.

### Run socket and host control socket

- **Framing** (fragment- and coalesce-safe): `[type: u8][length: u32 BE][payload]`.
  - Type `0x01`: UTF-8 JSON message, at most 1 MiB.
  - Type `0x02`: screencast frame, at most 4 MiB, as `[meta_len: u16][meta JSON][JPEG bytes]`.
  - A malformed type or length closes the connection.
- **Message order:**
  1. `hello` with the run token or control token, `channel_version` and `capabilities`;
  2. `subscribe {from_seq}`;
  3. the stream: `event {seq, event}`, `heartbeat`, `attendance {count}` from host to worker,
     `intervention.answer` and its D12 response, `cancel`, and the frame control messages
     `frames.start/stop`, `frame.ack`, `frames.cleared {generation}`.
- **Queues.** Each connection has two outbound queues. Control and events always flush before
  frames.
  - The **event queue** is bounded (8 MiB). Overflow disconnects that client, which reconnects and
    replays from the file, so nothing is lost.
  - The **frame queue** holds one frame; the newest replaces it.
  - Writes honor socket backpressure.
- **Authentication.** POSIX sockets live in a 0700 directory with 0600 files. Windows named pipes
  have unguessable names. On both, the **first message must carry the token** from the owner-only
  lease or host lock, and unauthenticated connections are closed without a reply.

### App ↔ host

- **HTTP:**
  - `GET /` and content-hashed assets;
  - `POST /session` exchanges a launch code for a session cookie plus a per-window capability;
  - `GET /a/<signed>`: short-lived signed artifact URLs for media and downloads.
- **WebSocket, JSON-RPC 2.0** (first message `auth {window_capability}`):
  - **Commands:** `command.invoke {invocation, displayed_effective}` returns
    `{invocation_id, state, position?, run_id?}`. It is idempotent per `invocation_id`.
  - **Queue:** `command.cancel`, `queue.list`, `queue.start`, `queue.discard`,
    `queue.resolve_review {choice}`.
  - **Reads:** `read.<name>` for each `read`-class command, returning that command's `--json`
    schema with cursor pagination where lists can grow.
  - **Subscriptions:** `run.subscribe {run_id, from_seq}`; `runs.subscribe`;
    `interventions.subscribe`, which also drives attendance (D5).
  - **Interventions:** `intervention.answer {intervention_id, decision}`, which returns the D12
    response.
  - **Frames:** `frames.subscribe {run_id}`.
  - **Credentials:** `secret.set {key}` (the value is sent once and never echoed), `secret.rm`,
    `secret.list`.
  - **Artifacts:** `artifact.url {run_id, path}` returns a signed URL for an allowlisted artifact.

### Surfaces and flow

- **Mission** is the start page: composer and live cockpit.
- **Ledger** lists all runs; each opens **Run result** (`/runs/<id>`) and **Audit**.
- **Inbox** has a badge in the top bar; the Bindu turns Rani while it has open items.
- **Settings** has Installation, Preferences, Models, Credentials, Browser, Sites and Data.
- **Health** shows doctor checks, host environment age and possible orphans.
- **Workflows, Templates, Schedules and Usage** are generated surfaces in the MVP.
- **`/gallery`** exists in development builds only.
- **`Ctrl/Cmd+K`** opens the palette everywhere.

### Artifacts and state (all additive)

- **Per run:**
  - `lease.json` (owner-only; holds the token and owned browser process identities; deleted after
    completion evidence is flushed);
  - `run-events.jsonl`;
  - `execution-receipt.json`;
  - `interventions.jsonl`;
  - `decisions/<confirmation_id>.json` (parked-decision claims);
  - `reconcile.lock` (transient).
- **Host state** under `<data-dir>/ui/`: `host.lock` (owner-only: PID, start token, port, control
  socket, control token), `slots.lock`, `invocations/`, `host.log`, `chrome-profile/`.
- **Sockets.** Unix sockets sit in a short owner-only directory, because socket paths are limited
  to about 104 bytes on macOS. Windows uses named pipes.
- **Paths.** Every path comes from `packages/core/src/browser/paths.ts` (memory → Project
  Structure).
- **Unchanged files.** `events.jsonl`, `runtime.jsonl`, `tool-calls.jsonl`, `manifest.json`,
  `brief.*` and `confirmations.jsonl` keep their shapes. Manifests gain the optional
  `executionState`.

### Protocol additions

- New schemas: `CommandRegistry`, `CommandInvocation`, `ExecutionReceipt`, `RunEvent`,
  `Intervention`, `RunLease`, the socket and RPC messages, `DecisionResponse`.
- Optional binding fields on `ConfirmationRequest`.
- `ConfirmationDecidedBy` gains `user_app`; `TerminationReason` gains `owner_lost`.
- `executionState` on manifests.

## 7. Security Considerations

Standing rules are in `memory.md` → Security. Plan-specific concerns, under the D18 threat model:

- **Sessions.**
  - The canonical origin is exactly `http://127.0.0.1:<port>`. Requests and WebSocket upgrades
    with any other `Host` are rejected, which defeats DNS rebinding.
  - Mutations and upgrades require that exact `Origin`. No CORS headers are sent.
  - `yantra ui` passes a **single-use launch code valid for 60 seconds** in the URL fragment. The
    app removes it with `history.replaceState` before anything else runs.
  - `POST /session` sets an `HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Path=/` cookie **and** returns a
    **per-window capability** (256-bit random). It is held in JavaScript memory only and required
    on every RPC (`auth` message) and every artifact URL signature.
  - A capability expires 5 minutes after its WebSocket closes, and after 12 hours absolute.
  - Request bodies and WebSocket messages are limited to 1 MiB.
  - A strict `Content-Security-Policy` (`default-src 'self'`) applies, and the app makes no
    third-party requests.
- **Artifacts.**
  - Only artifact types the registry marks **public** are served, through signed URLs that expire
    after 5 minutes and are bound to the path and window. Paths resolve with `realpath` inside the
    runs root.
  - **Never served:** `lease.json`, `reconcile.lock`, `decisions/` claim files (their content
    reaches the app only through typed reads), temporary files, sockets, `host.lock`,
    `invocations/`, browser profiles.
  - `Content-Type` comes from an allowlist, with `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. HTML artifacts
    are downloads only; the app renders results from JSON.
- **Run and control sockets.** Token authentication is mandatory on every OS (§6). On Windows,
  owner-only file protection relies on the user-profile directory's default ACL (the user, SYSTEM
  and Administrators). The plan states this rather than assuming POSIX modes.
- **Secrets.**
  - Credential writes run in-process and never reach argv; a test inspects spawned processes'
    command lines.
  - Responses list names only.
  - The canary-secret assertions cover **outbound and persisted** channels only: host→app
    messages, HTTP responses, worker→client socket messages, `run-events.jsonl`, receipts and
    `host.log`. The inbound credential submission necessarily contains the value and is excluded
    by design.
- **Consent provenance.** Decisions follow D12. `user_app` is stamped only for answers arriving
  over an authenticated host connection that relays an authenticated window. There is still no
  agent variant.
- **Screencast privacy** follows FEAT-069. Frames are never persisted and never sent to the model,
  so they fall outside the `context.screenshots` grant. Document this in
  `docs/features/safety-and-privacy.md`.
- **Untrusted page-derived text** (titles, quotes, URLs, model text) renders through React escaping
  and markdown with raw HTML disabled. External links carry `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.
- **The app window is not an automation target.** It has a dedicated profile and no remote
  debugging port (D10).

## 8. Architecture & Design (Plan-Specific)

### Process model

```
yantra ui ──control socket (token)──► App host  (one per machine: <data-dir>/ui/host.lock)
                                        │  HTTP + WebSocket on 127.0.0.1 ◄── Chrome --app window(s)
                                        │  reads in-process · invocations/ · slots.lock (D11)
                                        ▼  spawns shell-free, detached
               ┌──── worker = command handler + worker adapter (FEAT-072)
               │       claims invocation → claims lease → receipt → run-events.jsonl → run socket
               └──── worker …
yantra <cmd> in a terminal: same handler + terminal adapter; same lease, receipt, log and socket
yantra daemon: unchanged and hard zero-LLM; its runs also write leases; parked decisions use D12
```

### Dependency direction

- `protocol → core → agent → cli` is unchanged.
- `packages/ui` depends on `@yantra/protocol` **for types only**, and never imports core, agent or
  Node built-ins.
- `apps/web` depends on `@yantra/ui` and `@yantra/protocol`.
- `apps/cli` embeds the built `apps/web/dist` at build time; Turbo orders `apps/web#build` first.

### Event log contract (FEAT-063/064)

- **Single writer.** The process that owns the lease appends to `run-events.jsonl`. A reconciler
  may append only after winning the reconcile claim.
- **Persist before publish.** An event is appended (write completed) before it reaches renderers or
  sockets.
- **Flush points:** every intervention change, every terminal event, and otherwise every 50 events
  or 1 second.
- **Tail recovery.** Readers ignore a trailing partial line. Only the writer or reconciler truncates
  it before appending, and `seq` continues from the last valid line.
- **Atomic replay-to-live.** Because the writer also serves the socket, `subscribe` works on one
  event loop:
  1. register a buffering listener;
  2. take the watermark W (last committed `seq`);
  3. send file events from `from_seq` to W;
  4. flush buffered events above W;
  5. go live.

  Clients deduplicate by `seq`.

- **Reconciliation** (idempotent at every step):
  1. acquire `reconcile.lock`;
  2. re-verify the owner is dead by identity;
  3. if no terminal event exists, truncate any partial tail and append one `run_outcome` with
     `owner_lost`;
  4. update the manifest (`executionState: interrupted`; outcome per D7) with an atomic write;
  5. update the history index.

  A crash mid-reconcile is finished by the next reconciler, and only one terminal result ever
  exists.

- **Completion evidence before lease removal.** A worker flushes its terminal event and manifest
  before deleting `lease.json`. A reattached host derives outcomes from this evidence, never from an
  exit code it did not observe.

### Run lifecycle and displayed states

- **Execution:** `queued → reserved → starting → running ⇄ waiting-for-you → finished`.
- **Outcome:** `fulfilled | partial | handoff | failed | aborted`, plus `executionState:
interrupted` when the owner was lost.
- **Separate displayed conditions**, each with a next action:
  - **Disconnected**: the app lost its host connection.
  - **Worker not responding**: the run socket has had no heartbeat for 30 seconds.
  - **Engine stalled**: the existing FEAT-059 recovery events.
  - **Needs review**: D13 settings drift.
  - **Start outcome unknown**: D11.

### Reliability matrix

| Failure                                     | Behavior                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Worker crashes                              | Reconciliation writes the single terminal result (`owner_lost`); the host keeps serving                                                                                                                                                      |
| Worker hangs                                | "Worker not responding" after 30 s of no heartbeat; Stop offered                                                                                                                                                                             |
| User stops a run                            | Graceful: `cancel` over the socket → the same clean-abort path as `SIGINT`. If still alive after 10 s: forced termination of the identity-verified process tree (on Windows every signal is forceful), **always followed by reconciliation** |
| App window closes                           | Attendance drops (D5); workers continue; the host exits after 10 idle minutes once no window is connected and no invocation is reserved, spawning or queued                                                                                  |
| Browser connection drops                    | The app reconnects with backoff and resubscribes `from_seq`; no gaps, no duplicates                                                                                                                                                          |
| Host crashes                                | Workers continue (D6); D11 recovery on the next start; reattach with handshake (D17)                                                                                                                                                         |
| Host restarts with an older or newer worker | D17: attach if compatible, otherwise "live view unavailable" while the run continues                                                                                                                                                         |
| Owned Chrome orphaned                       | Reaped only after start-token identity verification through the existing lifecycle modules; uncertain identity keeps the ownership record and shows "possible orphan" in Health, never killed                                                |
| Recovery                                    | **Resume** only when the core resumability check (checkpoint exists, failure class permits) says so; **Run again** otherwise, warning when the prior run may have had external effects                                                       |

### Delivery milestones

Slices within the existing features. Feature specs break them into tasks.

- **Spikes first, in parallel:**
  - **S1**: glass and readability over a screencast (FEAT-069 task 1).
  - **S2**: worker and recovery on Windows, macOS and Linux. It covers detached spawn, host death
    and reattach, approval across reconnect, and orphan cleanup (FEAT-064 task 1).

  Either can force an architecture change, so both run before the cockpit is polished.

- **M1, read-only slice:**
  - the tokens and primitives the Ledger and results need (FEAT-061 partial);
  - read-class registry entries (FEAT-062 partial);
  - host, sessions and security suite (FEAT-065 partial);
  - Ledger, run results and Audit (FEAT-066).
- **M2, one deterministic live run.** A `research --no-llm` run end to end:
  - FEAT-072 seams for `research`;
  - FEAT-063 log;
  - FEAT-064 ownership;
  - FEAT-065 supervisor and launch ownership;
  - the FEAT-067 cockpit subset.
- **M3, one consent round trip.** A scripted fake-provider `do` with consent answered in the app and
  by `yantra confirm`, plus a parked scheduled run approved from the Inbox (FEAT-068).
- **M4, breadth:**
  - the live browser view (FEAT-069);
  - the full registry and parity (FEAT-062, FEAT-070);
  - onboarding, Health and Credentials (FEAT-071);
  - the remaining primitive catalogue (FEAT-061).

### Sequencing

1. **Can start at once, in parallel:** FEAT-061 (M1 subset), FEAT-062, S1 and S2.
2. **FEAT-072** after FEAT-062. **FEAT-063** can start alongside FEAT-072.
3. **FEAT-064** after FEAT-063 and S2.
4. **FEAT-065** after FEAT-061 (M1 subset), FEAT-062 and FEAT-064. Its read-only portion may begin
   once FEAT-062's read entries exist.
5. **FEAT-066** after FEAT-065's read-only portion.
6. **FEAT-067** after FEAT-063, FEAT-066 and FEAT-072. **FEAT-068** after FEAT-067.
7. **FEAT-069** (rest) after FEAT-067 and S1. **FEAT-070** after FEAT-062, FEAT-065, FEAT-066 and
   FEAT-072. **FEAT-071** after FEAT-070.

### Compatibility

- Existing artifacts remain readable by new code. New files are additive.
- New enum values are not readable by older executables (D7).
- **CLI-visible changes:**
  - `yantra ui`;
  - `confirm` answering live runs;
  - `ui.theme` and `ui.surfaces` preferences;
  - possible `busy` responses on locked writes;
  - dead-owner runs showing `interrupted` with an evidence-based outcome instead of `running`.
- `--help` output is byte-identical after FEAT-062.

### Risks

| Risk                                                                       | Mitigation                                                                                                                                                                             |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Handler refactor and registry extraction touch ~30 commands and 98 options | FEAT-072 migrates command by command; `--help` snapshots plus behavior characterization (same scenario through terminal and worker adapters yields identical artifacts and exit codes) |
| Glass over a live screencast is slow or illegible                          | S1 before the HUD; contrast guaranteed by the scrim floor, not sampling; automatic Solid fallback                                                                                      |
| Detached processes, pipes and identity differ by OS                        | S2 on all three OSes first; token auth mandatory; existing identity modules reused                                                                                                     |
| Lock contention surprises users                                            | Explicit `busy` with the holder's description; locks held only around read-modify-write                                                                                                |
| Design perfectionism delays value                                          | Milestones ship M1 before the full primitive catalogue                                                                                                                                 |

## 9. Coding Standards (Plan-Specific Overrides)

Memory's standards apply. Additions:

- **Handlers never touch the process.** Inside command handlers there is no `process.exit`, no
  `process.stdin.isTTY`, no direct stdout or stderr writes, and no `new CLIConnectorIO`. All of these
  arrive as dependencies (FEAT-072). A lint rule enforces it in `apps/cli/src/commands/`.
- **Read-modify-write of shared files goes through the core lock helpers** with unique temporary
  names (D14). A fixed `<path>.tmp` is a lint error in core.
- **Styling only through Drshya semantic utilities.** No raw palette utilities, arbitrary color
  values, or hex/`oklch()` literals in components. Inline `style` is allowed only for CSS custom
  properties carrying data.
- **Icons only from the semantic registry.** Importing `lucide-react` elsewhere is a lint error.
- **Interactive elements come from Drshya primitives** on React Aria; no `div` buttons or
  hand-rolled menus, dialogs or listboxes.
- **`packages/ui` imports no Node built-ins and nothing from `@yantra/core` or `@yantra/agent`**
  (import-boundary lint).
- **Function components and hooks only.** Live state comes from a `useSyncExternalStore` store over
  the event stream, with no global singletons (memory → Architecture).
- **Product words are the CLI's words**, rendered verbatim from protocol values.
- **Focus moves only on user action.** Live updates announce through a polite live region; they
  never steal focus.
- Tests live in mirrored `tests/` directories; `.tsx` is linted and type-checked repo-wide.

## 10. Testing Strategy (Plan-Specific)

Memory's testing rules apply. In particular: e2e and CLI suites resolve `@yantra/core` from built
`dist/`, real-Chrome cases need their own timeouts, timing is counted on stepped clocks, and the
repo-wide lint and typecheck are the gate.

- **Unit (Vitest):**
  - registry schemas and generation;
  - `parse`/`format` round-trip for every command;
  - `RunEvent`, `Intervention`, receipt and lease schemas, with old and new fixtures in both
    directions;
  - framing parser with fragmented, coalesced and malformed input;
  - attendance-ceiling and deadline computation on a stepped clock, including sleep and wake;
  - lock helpers;
  - Host/Origin/cookie/capability middleware.
- **Characterization (FEAT-072):** byte-identical `--help`; for each migrated command, the same
  scenario through the terminal adapter and the worker adapter produces identical artifacts, receipts
  and exit codes.
- **Launch ownership (FEAT-065, B1 evidence):**
  - simultaneous submissions;
  - lost RPC responses followed by retry of the same ID;
  - host kill before spawn, after spawn but before the claim, after the claim but before the lease,
    and after completion but before the response.

  Each case verifies one worker per invocation and at most two reserved-or-running slots, plus two
  concurrent resumes of one run.

- **Consent (FEAT-068, B2 evidence):**
  - app versus `yantra confirm` answering the same request;
  - an answer racing the timeout;
  - a repeated answer after reconnect;
  - a changed action on resume (denied with the binding blocker);
  - a second flagged step after resume;
  - the full park → grant from the Inbox → daemon pickup path remaining zero-LLM.
- **Event log (FEAT-063/064, I4 evidence):**
  - truncated tail;
  - kill between manifest and event writes;
  - simultaneous reconcilers producing exactly one terminal result;
  - emit during replay;
  - a slow reader overflowing and recovering by replay;
  - malformed lengths;
  - stalled frame acknowledgements not delaying control traffic.
- **Resources (FEAT-072, I1 evidence):** CLI and app writers updating `config.yaml` and
  `profile.yaml` concurrently lose no change; two runs selecting the same persistent browser
  profile; browser install during a run.
- **Invocation and receipt (I2 evidence):**
  - a reused host started from another directory;
  - preferences changed while queued, producing `needs_review`;
  - a missing or edited workflow;
  - historical runs without an invocation;
  - copied commands executed in real bash, PowerShell 5.1 and cmd with quotes, `$`, backticks,
    `%`, `^`, `!` and newlines.
- **Security suite (merge gate from FEAT-065):**
  - missing, replayed or expired launch codes and capabilities;
  - a session cookie presented without a capability, or from another loopback port's page;
  - foreign `Origin`; rebinding `Host`; cross-site form POST;
  - unauthenticated run or control socket;
  - attempts to fetch `lease.json` or other denied files;
  - artifact path traversal;
  - outbound canary scans.
- **Screencast (FEAT-069, I8 evidence):** delayed frames across latch set and clear; navigation;
  reconnect; multiple viewers; tab and target change; the deterministic secret fill.
- **Accessibility (I9 evidence):**
  - `axe-core` on every gallery state and app route;
  - keyboard-only approve and deny through the untimed path, with focus return;
  - 200% zoom and 320 CSS px reflow;
  - a manual NVDA pass on Windows and a VoiceOver smoke pass on macOS for the Inbox, GuardedSwitch
    and live timeline;
  - analytic contrast for glass text against pure black and pure white backdrops.
- **Run results (I11 evidence):**
  - a successful workflow with no synthesis;
  - a failure before a Brief exists;
  - an interrupted legacy run;
  - source and action citations;
  - legacy runs without evidence;
  - corrupt and missing artifacts;
  - unsupported old schemas;
  - a large run directory (50,000 events, multi-hundred-MB captures).
- **Compatibility (I6 evidence):** a host speaking to a previous `channel_version` worker fixture;
  refresh of stale app assets.
- **App e2e** (puppeteer-core): the M1–M3 milestone flows, in the `LLM_PROVIDER=none` dimension
  where applicable.
- **Parity (FEAT-070):** mapping completeness **and** real execution of every generated form against
  a sandboxed `YANTRA_HOME`.
- **Cross-platform:** run sockets, detached spawn, identity and cleanup on Windows, macOS and Linux
  CI.
- **Performance:** event latency worker → app p95 < 150 ms; screencast ≥ 5 fps with the app main
  thread under 15% of one core.

## 11. Logging Strategy (Plan-Specific)

Memory's logging rules apply (structured Pino, never secrets).

- **Host log** (`<data-dir>/ui/host.log`). It records:
  - host start and stop, with the environment capture time;
  - invocation state transitions (invocation ID, run ID, class);
  - worker claim and exit;
  - attach and reattach, with handshake versions;
  - reconciliation decisions;
  - drift reviews;
  - lock-busy responses;
  - security rejections, as counts with the rejected `Origin` host.

  It **never** records launch codes, cookies, capabilities, tokens, signed URLs, secret values or
  frames.

- **Runs.** `runtime.jsonl` gains:
  - `intervention_raised` and `intervention_resolved` (kind, decided_by, waited ms, D12 response);
  - `attendance_changed` (count only);
  - `attendance_ceiling_expired`;
  - `channel_attached` and `channel_detached` (client kind and version);
  - `settings_receipt_written`;
  - `reconciled` (by whom, evidence used).
- **Not logged:** individual heartbeats. A stall or "worker not responding" is logged once when
  detected.

## 12. Feature Scope and Acceptance

### FEAT-061: Drshya Foundations

**Scope.**

- **Tokens.** Tailwind v4 `@theme` in three tiers (values from `ui_brainstorm.md` §Color, with Ion's
  two fills):
  - primitive: fog, Ion, Jade, Amber, Crimson, Rani;
  - semantic: `bg`, `surface`, `sunken`, `ink`/`ink-2`/`ink-3`, `rule`/`rule-strong`, `accent`,
    `on-accent`, `accent-ink`, `signal-*`, `glass-*`;
  - component knobs.
- **Themes.** Light and dark through `prefers-color-scheme` plus `data-theme`. Solid mode through
  `data-surfaces` and `prefers-reduced-transparency`.
- **Glass with a guaranteed scrim floor.** Minimum tint opacities are computed so glass text meets
  4.5:1 against **any** backdrop between pure black and pure white. Sampling is regression evidence
  only.
- **Type and other tokens:**
  - self-hosted Archivo (widths 100 to 125) and Martian Mono (width 87.5);
  - radius, space and motion tokens;
  - reduced motion honored.
- **Icons.** The semantic icon registry and six custom glyphs on Lucide's grid.
- **Primitives on React Aria Components, grown per milestone.**
  - **M1:** Button, Link, Table (virtualized, cursor-paged), Tabs, Tooltip, Disclosure, Toast.
  - **Later:** TextField, NumberField, Checkbox, Switch, Select, ComboBox, Dialog, Popover, Menu.
- **Lint.** The raw-color and icon-import rules.
- **Gallery and harnesses.** A `/gallery` route, plus the screenshot and accessibility harness
  (`axe-core`).

**Acceptance.**

- Every primitive renders in the gallery in light and dark, Glass and Solid, with visual baselines.
- Every text pairing, including Ion on both themes, passes contrast. Glass text passes analytically
  against black and white.
- `axe-core` reports no violations in the gallery.
- Lint fails on a raw palette utility or a direct `lucide-react` import.
- The package has no import from core, agent or Node built-ins.
- Focus is visible everywhere.

### FEAT-062: Command Registry

**Scope.** A Zod-described registry in `@yantra/protocol` covering every command and subcommand:

- **Shape:** path and arguments; options with type, default, the precedence chain (naming env var
  and preference key), applicability and help.
- **Execution:** an option-dependent `execution` class (§6 table, including adapters and
  exemptions); `effect` (`none | local | external`) and `danger` (requires explicit confirmation in
  generated forms).
- **Form metadata:** input kinds (`text | enum | bool | duration | number | path(file|dir) |
workflow-ref | template-ref | run-ref | secret-input`) and option relations (`requires`,
  `conflicts`).
- **Results:** exit codes, `--json` schema reference.

It also provides:

- the commander tree generated from the registry, command by command, with handlers bound by path;
- `CommandInvocation` with `parse` and shell-aware `format` (§6).

**Acceptance.**

- `--help` is byte-identical for every command.
- `format(parse(argv))` round-trips for every command.
- Copied commands execute correctly in bash, PowerShell 5.1 and cmd (or cmd is marked unavailable
  with the reason).
- Every command has an execution class.
- No command registers an option it cannot act on (a test asserts a consumer per option).
- Unmigrated commands appear only on a dated allowlist that FEAT-070 empties.

### FEAT-072: Command Handler Seams, Execution Receipts & Shared-Resource Locks

**Scope.**

- **Handler dependencies.** Every handler takes, as explicit dependencies:
  - a connector;
  - confirmation and install-offer gateways;
  - an input collector (prompts, secure input);
  - output (renderer and `--json` envelope sink);
  - completion (result and exit code, instead of `process.exit`);
  - an abort signal;
  - a settings resolver.
- **Adapters.** The terminal adapter in `bin.ts` supplies TTY behavior exactly as today. The worker
  adapter supplies socket-backed gateways, the attendance-aware interactive flag, and a result
  transport: `result {exit_code, envelope}` or `error {exit_code, code, message, remediation}`.
- **`init` service.** `init` becomes an application service with a pluggable answer collector:
  terminal prompts now, browser answers in FEAT-071.
- **Receipts.** Every run (CLI, worker, daemon) writes `execution-receipt.json` (D13).
- **Locks.** Core lock helpers keyed to config, profile, workflow, template, schedule registry and
  persistent browser profile, with unique temporary files (D14). Managed-browser operations keep
  their reservations.
- **Lint.** The handler purity rule (§9).

**Acceptance.**

- Characterization (§10): terminal and worker adapters produce identical artifacts, receipts and exit
  codes for each migrated command.
- No handler references `process.exit`, `isTTY` or stdout directly.
- Concurrent CLI and app writers lose no configuration or profile change.
- A second run on a busy persistent profile gets `busy` or waits in the queue.
- Receipts contain no secret values and no full environment (canary).
- `init` answers given through the service produce the same files as today's wizard.

### FEAT-063: Unified Run-Event Stream

**Scope.**

- **The union.** A `RunEvent` union in `@yantra/protocol`, with `schema_version`. It covers:
  - the existing `TaskEvent` kinds;
  - the `AgentProgressEvent` variants, promoted from `@yantra/agent` and re-exported there:
    `recovery`, `progress`, `assistant_text`, `tool_started`, `tool_finished`,
    `contract_declared`, `capability_gap`;
  - new variants: `goal_echo`, `receipt_written`, `budget_snapshot`, `artifact_saved`,
    `intervention_raised`, `intervention_resolved`, `run_outcome`;
  - deterministic `ask`/`research` phase events (search, per-source fetch result, extract,
    synthesize).
- **Emission.** `ConnectorIO` emits the union.
- **The log.** `run-events.jsonl` follows the §8 contract: single writer, persist-before-publish,
  flush points, tail recovery.
- **Schema variants.** `owner_lost` and `user_app` added with fixtures in both directions.
- **Renderers.** The terminal and JSON renderers consume the union with unchanged output.

**Acceptance.**

- Every live event a CLI run shows today has a counterpart.
- `seq` is gap-free.
- Golden terminal and `--json` output is unchanged.
- A truncated tail recovers.
- A canary secret never appears in the log.
- New code reads every old fixture.

### FEAT-064: Run Ownership, Channel & Reconciliation

**Scope.**

- **Task 1 is spike S2:** detached spawn, host death and reattach, approval across reconnect, and
  orphan cleanup on three OSes, with a written report.
- **Leases.** Every run (CLI, worker, daemon) exclusively creates `lease.json` containing:
  - its own PID and start token, and the identities of the browser processes it owns;
  - the socket address and run token;
  - heartbeat time and execution class.
- **Run socket.** The §6 framing, queues, handshake and authentication, and the atomic
  replay-to-live watermark (§8).
- **Worker.** The detached worker entry (`apps/cli/dist/worker.js`) runs a `CommandInvocation`
  through the FEAT-072 worker adapter. One spawn helper covers all OSes: detached, shell-free, no
  inherited stdio, `windowsHide`.
- **Reconciliation.** The §8 algorithm, run at host start, at CLI run start and in `yantra list`.
  Execution state stays separate from outcome (D7).
- **Cleanup.** Owned-browser cleanup through `process-identity` and `process-lifecycle`, killing only
  identity-verified processes. Forced termination is always followed by reconciliation.
- **Guard.** `config data-dir` refuses while live leases or a host lock exist (D15).

**Acceptance.**

- A killed run reconciles to exactly one terminal result with `executionState: interrupted`, even
  with simultaneous reconcilers.
- A reused PID is never treated as an owner.
- An uncertain browser identity is never killed.
- A second client attaches and replays with no gaps or duplicates, including while events are
  emitted during replay.
- A slow client cannot delay control traffic.
- An unauthenticated client receives nothing.
- A previous-`channel_version` fixture yields "live view unavailable" without aborting the worker.
- All of the above pass on Windows, macOS and Linux.

### FEAT-065: App Host & `yantra ui`

**Scope.**

- **Command.** `yantra ui` (§6, D10).
- **Host.**
  - Single-instance, with `host.lock` and a token-authenticated control socket.
  - HTTP and WebSocket JSON-RPC on `127.0.0.1`.
- **Sessions (§7).** Launch codes, per-window capabilities, signed artifact URLs and expiry.
- **Launch ownership (D11).**
  - Invocation records, the slot lock and the limit of two.
  - The worker claim handshake.
  - Recovery states, including `never_started` and `start_unknown`.
- **Queue drift review (D13).**
- **Attendance relay to workers (D5).**
- **Stale-asset detection (D17).**
- **Idle exit** (§8).
- **Reads.** In-process `read.*` with cursor pagination. Change detection combines lease scanning,
  history-index change polling every 2 seconds, and filesystem watch hints, so CLI and daemon changes
  appear without a reload.
- **Preferences.** `ui.theme` and `ui.surfaces`.
- **Window launcher.** The Chrome `--app` launcher, with a profile under
  `<data-dir>/ui/chrome-profile`.
- **`apps/web` skeleton.** App shell, top bar, Bindu, navigation, and preferences applied. It is
  built and embedded into the CLI package.
- **The security suite.**

**Acceptance.**

- `yantra ui` opens or reuses a host. `--print`, `--json` and the no-Chromium exit 3 behave as
  specified.
- All §10 launch-ownership and security evidence passes.
- Killing the host mid-run leaves the worker running, and a new host reattaches.
- A host with zero windows does not count as attending.
- The app makes no third-party request.

### FEAT-066: Run Results & Audit

**Scope.**

- **Ledger.** History index plus file scan, with cursor pagination and filters on outcome, mode, date
  and text. It shows live runs and the states from §8.
- **Run result route `/runs/<id>`.**
  - **When a Brief or document exists:** overview, findings, sections (raw HTML off), condition
    statuses, cited rows, Sources and Also consulted, captures, notices.
  - **When none exists:** outputs, terminal reason, notices, `report.md` and artifacts.
- **Evidence.**
  - A source citation `[n]` opens the EvidencePane with its quote.
  - An action citation `A<n>` opens an ActionEvidence panel: action, value-free target identity,
    verification verdict, capture link.
  - Missing or legacy evidence shows an explicit "not recorded for this run" state.
- **Audit.** From the audit builder.
- **Artifact registry as a public allowlist** (§7), with bounded and windowed viewers: a JSONL
  viewer with virtualization and size caps; raw files over the cap offer "Show in folder".
- **Resilience.** Corrupt, missing, legacy and very large artifacts fail per item, never per page.
- **Instruments.** OutcomeBadge, RequirementList, ConditionTable, CitationChip, EvidencePane,
  ActionEvidence, CaptureGallery, ProtectedValue, EventInspector.

**Acceptance.**

- Every golden Brief renders.
- A successful zero-synthesis workflow, a pre-Brief failure and an interrupted legacy run each render
  a complete result page.
- Every cited claim opens its evidence in one click.
- Denied artifacts are unreachable.
- A 50,000-event run stays responsive.
- ProtectedValue never shows a value or its length.
- Outcome words match the CLI exactly.

### FEAT-067: Mission — Composer & Live Run Screen

**Scope.**

- **Composer.**
  - Modes Ask, Research, Do and Run (workflow picker).
  - Options generated from the registry for the selected command only, each showing its effective
    value and source.
  - Template selection.
  - It submits `{invocation, displayed_effective}`.
  - `do` is unavailable, with reason and fix, when no provider is configured.
- **Cockpit.**
  - Top bar: Bindu, mode, goal echo, elapsed time, BudgetGauges, Stop.
  - Understood: contract summary, ContractRing, RequirementList.
  - Engine: RunTimeline.
  - CliTwin with shell-aware Copy.
  - Glass over a neutral backdrop until FEAT-069.
- **Announcements and states.**
  - A polite live region announces contract revisions, interventions and outcomes, not individual
    tool calls.
  - The §8 states (queued, starting, waiting for you, disconnected, worker not responding, engine
    stalled, needs review, start outcome unknown), each with its next action.
- **Finish.** A View Transition to the run result.
- **Recovery.**
  - **Resume** only when resumable.
  - **Run again** with current or prior settings (D13), warning when the prior run had verified
    actions or allowed submission.

**Acceptance.**

- A `research --no-llm` and a scripted fake-provider `do` show every `RunEvent` in an instrument or
  the inspector.
- The CLI twin, pasted into the default shell, starts the identical command.
- No inapplicable option appears.
- Stop is graceful.
- A reload mid-run resumes with no gaps.
- Screen-reader output stays meaningful during a fast run.

### FEAT-068: Interventions & Notifications

**Scope.**

- **First, verify** the narrowed gap from §15 (binding and atomicity), then implement D12 in core.
- **The model.** The `Intervention` protocol model, with kinds `consent | handoff | input |
takeover`.
  - **Decision states** are authoritative and owned by the worker or the parked-decision claim:
    `pending → granted | denied | timed_out`.
  - **Notification attempts** are recorded separately per channel (app, desktop) as `attempted`,
    `delivered`, `failed` or `unsupported`. They never gate a decision.
  - Persistence: `interventions.jsonl` and `notifications.jsonl`.
- **MVP behavior per kind:**
  - **consent** pauses and continues on approval;
  - **handoff** is terminal, with its blocker and recovery;
  - **input** records missing items from a partial run, and the Inbox offers **Run again with this
    added**;
  - **takeover** exists in the schema and resolves as a handoff.
- **Attendance (D5).** Window attendance heartbeats, cumulative ceiling and absolute deadlines.
- **GuardedSwitch.** A pointer hold for mouse and touch, plus an **untimed review-then-confirm path**
  for keyboard and assistive input. Both use the same server checks. Deny is the default, the
  remaining time is shown, and focus returns afterwards.
- **Inbox.** Live interventions; parked scheduled runs, approved through the D12 claim and the
  binding-checked resume; expired and handed-off items with recovery; `needs_review` and
  `start_unknown` invocations.
- **`yantra confirm`.** Answers live runs through D12.
- **Desktop "needs you" notification.** Sent by the worker through `SinkNotifier`, best-effort and
  tracked.

**Acceptance.**

- All §10 consent evidence passes.
- An answer in the app records `user_app`; `yantra confirm` records `user_cli_confirm`. Replay keeps
  the original provenance.
- A live host with zero windows and a non-empty queue does not stop the ceiling.
- A `timeout_ms: null` workflow request expires unattended at 15 cumulative minutes (stepped clock)
  and exits 4 with the item recorded.
- Agentic waits never exceed `agent.confirm_timeout`.
- Keyboard-only approve and deny work without timing.
- A failed desktop notification leaves the decision state unaffected.

### FEAT-069: Live Browser View

**Scope.**

- **Task 1 is spike S1:** 5–10 fps under four glass panels, measuring frame time, CPU and contrast,
  with a report.
- **Protection** is defined as: the run's `SensitiveScreenLatch` is set (agent secret fills); **or**
  a deterministic secret or masked-value fill is in progress (this feature adds the latch to the
  deterministic fill paths); **or** a FEAT-056 protected control has focus.
- **Frames.**
  - Each frame carries `{generation, document_epoch, captured_at}`.
  - The worker increments the generation on protection set or clear, top-level navigation, target
    change and stream restart, and drops frames from older generations.
  - When protection starts, it sends `frames.cleared`; the host and app discard the displayed
    image and show "Protected screen — hidden".
  - After protection clears, frames resume only from a capture taken after the new generation
    began.
- **Task page.** The agent controller's active page, following the existing popup policy. A switch
  counts as a target change.
- **Delivery.** Frames go through the latest-wins frame queue (§6). They are never persisted and
  never sent to the model.
- **Other views:**
  - a headed-run state ("Running in a visible window");
  - a text alternative (current host, page title and the RunTimeline);
  - BrowserViewport behind the HUD, with automatic Solid over budget.
- **Documentation.** Update `docs/features/safety-and-privacy.md`.

**Acceptance.**

- All §10 screencast evidence passes.
- No frame from a protected generation is displayed after protection starts, including delayed and
  multi-viewer cases.
- No frame file exists in the run directory.
- The rates and CPU budget are met, or Solid engages.

### FEAT-070: Parity Manifest, Command Palette & Generated Surfaces

**Scope.**

- **Parity manifest.** Maps every registry command, `RunEvent` kind and artifact type to a surface,
  instrument, adapter or written exemption (`--json`, `--open`, `config data-dir`, `ui`).
- **Palette.** `Ctrl/Cmd+K` accepting CLI syntax, with shell-aware "Copy as command".
- **Generated surfaces.** Built from registry presentation metadata and `--json` schemas:
  - Settings: Installation, Preferences with provenance, Models, Browser (install and update keep
    their consent step), Sites, Data (D15 instructions);
  - Workflows, Templates, Schedules, Usage (table), Daemon.
- **Adapters.** `config edit`, `open`, `daemon start/stop`.
- **Danger.** Commands marked `danger` require explicit confirmation in their forms.

**Acceptance.**

- The parity test passes with zero unmapped entries and an empty allowlist.
- **Every generated form is executed** against a sandboxed `YANTRA_HOME`, and its CLI twin equals
  what a terminal user would type.
- The palette executes any parseable command and explains one it cannot parse.

### FEAT-071: Onboarding, Health & Credentials

**Scope.**

- **Onboarding.** Through the shared `init` service with a browser answer collector: provider,
  credential reference, model, storage, search-provider key, sensitive-context grants. Questions are
  explicit, with no inference, and the flow is skippable.
- **Health.**
  - Each `doctor` check with status, detail and engineered remediations only.
  - Smoke checks run as a run-class worker.
  - It also shows host environment age (D13) and possible orphans (§8).
- **Credentials.** Names only. Set and remove run in-process (D2) through a write-only field.
  References are shown with ProtectedValue.

**Acceptance.**

- Onboarding produces the same `config.yaml` and `profile.yaml` as terminal `init` for the same
  answers.
- Every `doctor` check renders.
- Outbound canary scans pass for set, list and remove.
- No credential value ever reaches the app after submission.
- No credential appears in any process's argv.

## 13. Phase 2 (Deferred and Documented)

Each item lists what the MVP lays down so Phase 2 is an extension, not a redesign.

- **Live takeover.** For a captcha, login or multi-factor challenge, the run pauses with a
  `takeover` intervention. You solve it yourself in the live view (pointer and key input forwarded
  through CDP `Input.*`), press **Done**, and the agent re-observes and continues. Yantra never
  solves or bypasses a challenge itself (memory → General).
  - _MVP lays down:_ the `takeover` kind, run sockets, frame generations and protection.
  - _Needs:_ input forwarding with protection rules for input, and an agent pause/resume contract
    across a human action.
- **`ask_user` for missing information.** The run pauses with an `input` intervention and continues
  with your answer, treated like a goal-supplied value (attested, sanitized, FEAT-FP-008 masking,
  never a secret-shaped literal).
  - _MVP lays down:_ the `input` kind and "Run again with this added".
  - _Needs:_ a tool-catalog change and a prompt-version bump.
- **Desktop notifications for finished or failed runs**, sent only when the app is not focused.
  _MVP lays down:_ tracked notification attempts.
- **Live view of CLI-launched runs.** CLI runs already serve a run socket (FEAT-064); this adds
  attach from the app, read-only first.
- **Compact density.** It adds `ui.density` only when Compact renders, so the preference is never a
  dead control.
- **Target brackets on the live view.** Needs a viewport-relative element box on `A<n>` action
  evidence (value-free).
- **Bespoke studios:**
  - Workflow studio;
  - Recorder and web annotate (needs a `yantra record` command first);
  - Schedules timeline;
  - Template editor;
  - Usage charts;
  - Provenance thread graph.

## 14. Success Criteria

- The parity test passes with zero unmapped commands, event kinds or artifact types, and every
  generated form executes.
- A non-terminal user completes a first `ask` within two minutes of `yantra ui` on a configured
  install, and a `do` with one consent, without opening a terminal.
- Every cited claim opens its evidence in one click; every run, with or without a Brief, has a
  complete result page.
- Killing any one process (worker, host or window) loses no committed local record. Each run either
  completes or ends with exactly one honest terminal result and a valid recovery action, and no
  invocation launches twice.
- Consent is decided exactly once per request, by a human or a timeout, and is never replayed onto a
  different action.
- The localhost security suite and outbound canary scans pass on Windows, macOS and Linux.
- Event latency p95 < 150 ms; live view ≥ 5 fps within budget, or Solid engages automatically.
- WCAG 2.2 AA in both themes, on glass and solid. Consent works by keyboard and assistive input
  without timing.

## 15. Open Questions

- **Exact field shapes** of the deterministic `ask`/`research` phase events (FEAT-063), kept bounded
  and sanitized like agent progress events.
- **Thresholds to confirm against real runs:**
  - heartbeat 5 s, "not responding" 30 s;
  - host idle exit 10 minutes;
  - flush cadence 50 events or 1 second;
  - capability expiry 5 minutes after disconnect and 12 hours absolute.
- **Edge as the UI window on Windows** when Chrome is absent: confirm `--app` behavior and profile
  location per OS (FEAT-065).
- **Visual-regression baselines:** per-OS or Linux-only in CI (FEAT-061).
- **Parked-run consent: the narrowed, verified gap.** `resolveParkedRun` and the daemon's
  `PreGrantedConfirmationGateway` do implement park → grant → zero-LLM pickup. Two things are
  missing, and both are D12 work in FEAT-068:
  1. the grant is not **bound** to the approved action (the gateway approves the first request it
     sees);
  2. `confirm` decides with a non-atomic check-then-append.

  A second flagged step after resume is already denied. The broad "is the flow complete?" question
  from the first draft is withdrawn.

Every finding in [`plan_critique_ui.md`](./reviews/plan_critique_ui.md) was verified against source
and accepted. None was rejected.

| **B2** consent atomicity and binding           | D12 (worker as sole authority, D12 responses, parked-decision claims, action binding, provenance on replay); FEAT-068 scope; §15 narrowed                                                                         |
| **I1** concurrent writers, relocation deadlock | D14 (core locks, unique temporary files, `busy`, persistent-profile exclusivity); D15 (relocation exemption with CLI steps); FEAT-072                                                                             |
| **I2** "same argv" insufficient                | D13 (invocation versus receipt, resolve at start, drift review, Run again choices, reconstruction); shell-aware format and shell-free spawn (§6, FEAT-062)                                                        |
| **I3** handler boundary                        | D16 and new **FEAT-072** (explicit dependencies, adapters, `init` service, characterization); full execution-class table (§6); `--agent-smoke` corrected                                                          |
| **I4** event log and transport contract        | §8 event log contract; §6 framing, size limits, bounded and prioritized queues; durability promise stated in §1                                                                                                   |
| **I5** attendance versus host liveness         | D5 rewritten (window or terminal attendance, cumulative ceiling, absolute deadlines, sleep and wake); notification attempts separate from decisions (FEAT-068)                                                    |
| **I6** compatibility limits                    | D7 rewritten (`owner_lost`, separate execution state, both-direction fixtures, stated backward limit); D17 handshake, incompatible-worker message, stale assets                                                   |
| **I7** loopback trust boundaries               | D18 threat model; per-window capabilities, signed artifact URLs, 60-second launch codes, expiry, body limits; public-artifact allowlist; Windows control-channel policy; canary scope corrected (§7)              |
| **I8** screencast safety                       | FEAT-069 protection definition including deterministic fills, frame generations, `frames.cleared`, fresh-generation gating, independent backpressure                                                              |
| **I9** accessibility                           | Untimed review-then-confirm path; polite announcements; focus rules (§9); analytic scrim floor (FEAT-061); `axe-core`, keyboard, reflow and screen-reader checks (§10)                                            |
| **I10** process identity and force             | Identity-verified cleanup reusing existing modules; graceful cancel versus forced termination plus reconciliation; completion evidence before lease removal; "worker not responding" versus "engine stalled" (§8) |
| **I11** runs without a Brief                   | Run-result route for every run; Resume gated by resumability; ActionEvidence and legacy states (FEAT-066, FEAT-067)                                                                                               |
